Why go: Ang Thong on your own speedboat

On a shared tour, the boat sets the pace. On a private speedboat, you do. You can stay an extra hour at the reef, skip the viewpoint climb for more kayaking, or spend the afternoon on a beach the big groups only pass. You also choose who is on board, which matters for families with toddlers, groups celebrating something, photographers and anyone who wants a day without strangers. The price is 33,000 THB for the whole boat, with captain, crew, fuel, snorkel gear, kayaks, water and soft drinks.

The park is the same one the shared tours visit: 42 limestone islands about 30 km west of Koh Samui, around 102 km² of sea and land, with the headquarters on Koh Wua Talab (Wua Ta Lap). The two classic stops are the Emerald Lake on Koh Mae Ko, a cliff-ringed saltwater lagoon seen from a platform at the top of 15–20 minutes of steep wooden steps, and the 500 m viewpoint trail on Koh Wua Talab, 25–30 minutes up with ropes near the top. Snorkelling is at a reef the captain picks for the day's wind and tide, often around Koh Sam Sao, Koh Wao or Koh Tai Plao. The crossing takes about an hour, and the boat is out for about 8 hours.

As a guide to value: private 35 ft speedboats to Ang Thong are widely advertised on Samui at around 50,000–61,000 THB per day in 2026, depending on season. Our boat costs 33,000 THB per boat all year. Lunch and land transfers are optional, so you only pay for what you want.

Three ways to plan the day

  • Classic: Emerald Lake, then Koh Wua Talab for the viewpoint or the beach, kayaking, a snorkel stop and lunch. The same highlights as the shared tour, at your speed.
  • Snorkel-heavy: skip one climb, add a second or third reef, and finish with a long swim off a quiet beach.
  • Early start: leave Samui around 07:00 to arrive as the park opens at 08:00 and reach the Emerald Lake before the shared boats, then take a slow lunch while they are at the busy stops.

Who this tour is for

  • Groups of up to 10 who want the park on their own terms.
  • Families with very young children who need nap time, shade and their own schedule.
  • Photographers, honeymooners and birthday or proposal trips.
  • Groups where some want to climb and others want to swim: the captain can split the day.

Who should choose another tour

  • Two or three people on a budget: the VIP tour (4,500 THB per adult, only 15 guests) gives most of the comfort for less.
  • Want the cheapest Ang Thong day: the big boat or the speedboat tour.
  • Want a shorter private trip: the Pig Island private speedboat (11,950 THB per boat).
  • Larger group: see our private speedboat and catamaran charter pages.
  • Pregnant or with back problems: the crossing is open sea; we don't advise a speedboat.

What to bring

  • Cash for the park fee: 300 THB per foreign adult, 150 THB per child aged 3–14, paid on entry.
  • Food and drinks if you prefer a picnic to a restaurant stop (a cool box is fine; avoid glass).
  • Swimwear, towels, reef-safe sunscreen, hats and sunglasses.
  • Shoes with grip for the viewpoint trail.
  • Dry bags for phones and cameras.
  • Passport numbers for the accident insurance.

Good to know

  • Season: Ang Thong closes every year 1 November–15 December and reopens on 16 December. February to April is calmest; May to September is good most days; October is choppier. December to February is peak season with park quotas, so reserve the boat early.
  • Weather: rain alone doesn't cancel; strong wind and waves do. If we cancel for safety, you choose a full refund or a new date. Check windy.com and our tide and sea conditions pages.
  • No one-way drop-offs: the boat returns to Koh Samui. We can't drop you on Koh Phangan or elsewhere at the end of the day.
  • Park hours: the park is open 08:00–17:00, so the boat leaves the park by late afternoon.
  • Park rules: no swimming in the Emerald Lake, no fires, no feeding wildlife, no touching coral. Sunscreens with oxybenzone, octinoxate, 4-MBC or butylparaben are banned in Thai marine national parks.
  • Children: children's life jackets are always on board and children wear them at all times on the boat.
  • Drones: national parks require prior Department of National Parks permission, plus CAAT/NBTC registration.

Pickup and meeting point

Land transfers are optional. Most private guests come to the pier themselves; we send the pier location on WhatsApp when you book. If you would like a hotel transfer, ask us for the price when you book. Hotel transfers cover the main areas of Koh Samui, and remote areas such as Nathon, Lipa Noi, Taling Ngam, Bang Kao and Thong Krut cost 400 THB per person return. The start time is agreed when you book; a 09:00 departure is typical.
